description:
Who We Are



Founded in 1994, Surveying And Mapping, LLC (SAM) is a nationwide leader in geospatial and construction-phase solutions. With more than 50 offices and 1,600 professionals, we deliver the scale, technology, and expertise needed to support projects of any size. SAM streamlines project delivery through a single, coordinated team, offering in-house capabilities across land surveying, aerial mapping, subsurface utility engineering (SUE), utility coordination (UC), GIS, BIM, and construction engineering inspection (CEI).

 

By combining advanced technology, digital workflows, and decades of experience, we provide accurate, actionable data that helps clients move critical infrastructure projects forward with confidence. At SAM, you'll be part of a team that values innovation, growth, and the opportunity to make a tangible impact on the built environment.

 
Your Impact at SAM

SAM's Digital & Data Services group helps electric utilities turn complex infrastructure data into trusted, governed, and interoperable network models. We advise transmission and distribution utilities on how to manage their electrical network models across the full lifecycle—planned, designed, as-built, as-operated, and retired—and how to evolve from fragile, point-to-point model exchanges to governed model flows across GIS, asset management, planning, protection, and operations systems.

We are looking for a mid-level consultant to join SAM's Digital and Data Services division, with a primary goal of contributing to our Network Model Management (NMM) practice ideally in the areas of electric and gas utility industry. You will support client-facing engagements that include current-state assessments, target-state architecture, data governance design, integration delivery, and roadmap execution. You will work alongside senior architects and utility subject-matter experts to deliver practical, high-value outcomes for clients modernizing their grid data foundations.

This is a consulting role. You will contribute directly to the kinds of projects our team delivers today: network model management maturity assessments, vendor selection and RFP support, canonical data modeling, validation and quality-gate design, and integration flows connecting systems such as ESRI Utility Network, Work and Asset Management, EMS, ADMS, DERMS, Network Planning, and SCADA platforms.

Support client engagements focused on network model management, model governance, enterprise data integration, and digital transformation initiatives for electric and/or gas utilities.Help assess current-state model sources, consumers, ownership, and pain points (with emphasis on networks and assets) and translate findings into clear recommendations.Contribute to target-state architecture and canonical model design, including data flows between GIS, EAM, network planning, design, operations, protection, and analytics systems.Develop and document data governance artifacts: ownership and stewardship models, quality rules, workflow design, lineage, and lifecycle management.Design and help implement model validation, transformation, and publication patterns that produce traceable, trusted outputs for consuming systems.Assist with vendor evaluations, RFP development, requirements definition, and implementation roadmaps.Produce clear, client-ready deliverables—assessments, diagrams, requirements documents, and presentations—for both technical and executive audiences.Collaborate with SAM geospatial, engineering, and integration teams to connect field/GIS reality, enterprise asset data, and electrical model governance. 
What You Bring to SAM

4–8 years of professional experience in the electric utility industry or in consulting/technology roles serving electric utilities.Strong preference for hands-on experience in electric transmission & distribution (T&D) utilities, specifically focused on networks and asset subject areas within network planning, design, or operations business functions.Working knowledge of one or more core utility domains: transmission or distribution network modeling, GIS, asset/EAM systems, planning, protection, EMS/SCADA, or operations.Familiarity with how utility systems exchange model and asset data, and an understanding of the challenges created by point-to-point integrations and manual reconciliation.Strong analytical skills, with the ability to profile data, identify quality issues, and document processes and requirements clearly.Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce professional deliverables and present to client stakeholders.Comfort working in a collaborative, client-facing consulting environment with shifting priorities.Bachelor's degree in engineering (electrical engineering preferred), computer science, information systems, geospatial science, or a related field—or equivalent professional experience.Willingness to travel to client sites as project needs require (typically light to moderate).Desired Experience (Preferred, Not Required)Experience with or a working understanding of the IEC Common Information Model (CIM), including CIM profiles, extensions, or CIM-based model exchange. Candidates with genuine curiosity and a desire to grow their CIM expertise are strongly encouraged to apply.Exposure to network model management systems (NMMS) or model-management workflows across transmission and/or distribution for both electric and gas.Hands-on experience with utility platforms such as GIS (e.g. ESRI Utility Network, GE Smallworld), Asset Management (e.g. IBM Maximo, SAP/PM), Network Analysis Tools (e.g. Siemens PSS/E, Siemens CAPE/APA, ASPEN, CYME, DNV Synergi, Digsilent PowerFactory), EMS (e.g. AspenTech, GE, Siemens, ABB), ADMS (e.g. AspenTech, GE, Siemens, Schneider, Oracle, ACS, Hitachi), DERMS, or MDMS.Experience with system- and data integration patterns—API/event design, transformation, and validation automation.Experience with data governance frameworks, semantic modeling, or metadata management.Consulting experience delivering assessments, roadmaps, or implementation support for utility clients.Familiarity with DER integration, advanced analytics, or digital twin use cases in a grid context. 

 
Our Perks

Health and Wellness Benefits: BlueCross BlueShield health insurance coverage begins the month after your hire date, with dental plans available and free vision coverage for employees, company-paid premiums for Long-term disability/Life Insurance (with HSA + FSA plans), SAM Cares program focused on holistic well-beingFinancial Benefits: Employee Referral Rewards Program of $1K, $2,500 or $5K, Fidelity retirement plans with a 5% company match, tuition reimbursement, optional cellphone stipendWork-Life Balance: Paid time off including vacation/sick/holidays, parental leave to support familiesProfessional Development: Customized career development plan for licensing and certifications, Project Manager Business Academy, CAD Training Program, Individual Development Plans/Career Check-Ins, SAM WINS - our initiative for women-focused leadership and development, Milestone Anniversary Recognition, SAMbassador mentorship programPerks and Discounts: Access to “Perks at Work” for discounts on wellness + travel + leisure and everyday purchases, company-sponsored events, free office snacksCulture and Awards/Achievements: SAM Named 2026 Top Workplace USA for the fourth Year; 2026 SAM Ranks No. 92 on ENR Top 500 Design Firms

About This Opportunity Risepoint partners with leading universities to expand access to high-quality online education, and Partner Strategy & Analytics team sits at the center of how those partnerships grow and perform. We're looking for a Marketing & Operations Analytics Manager who can turn complex, full-funnel partner data — from lead generation through yield — into the strategic narrative that shapes how Risepoint invests in and grows its portfolio of partner institutions. This role is built for someone who thrives at the intersection of rigorous analysis and cross-functional leadership. You'll own analytical workstreams end-to-end, from framing the right question to delivering the insight that moves a decision, while partnering closely with Integrated Marketing, Channel Marketing, Partner Management, and Operations teams. You'll be expected to spot the data quality issue before it becomes a stakeholder problem, build the pipelines that make partner performance monitoring reliable, and use AI-assisted tools like Claude and Databricks Genie to work faster without ever outsourcing your judgment. As the team grows, you'll also start building and coaching the analysts around you — this is a role with real room to grow into people leadership. If you want a seat where your analysis directly informs how a national portfolio of university partnerships is managed and grown, this is that seat. The Impact You Will Make You'll be the analytical backbone behind partner growth strategy. Your work on enrollment funnel performance — lead gen through yield — will directly shape the conversations and decisions that determine how Risepoint supports long-term partner growth. You'll protect the integrity of the data leadership relies on. By catching errors, discontinuities, and reconciliation gaps before they surface downstream, you'll build a level of trust in the numbers that lets stakeholders move faster and with more confidence. You'll build infrastructure that outlasts any single analysis. The pipelines and reporting workflows you design — in partnership with BI and data engineering — will become the foundation partner performance monitoring runs on well beyond your own day-to-day work. You'll set the pace for how the team works. By embedding tools like Claude and Databricks Genie into daily practice, you'll help define what an AI-first analytical function actually looks like at Risepoint — faster analysis, sharper communication, same rigor. You'll turn data into decisions. Through the KPIs you establish and the insights you translate into clear recommendations, you'll give executives and department heads a direct line from performance data to action. Position Summary

The Automotive Robotics Engineer is responsible for the design, development, commissioning, optimization, and continuous improvement of robotic welding for automated assembly systems supporting automotive ladder frame, subframe, crossmember, and chassis assembly operations. The successful candidate will lead manufacturing engineering activities from concept through production launch, ensuring robotic systems achieve safety, quality, throughput, and cost objectives while meeting customer and APQP requirements.

This position works closely with Product Engineering, Controls Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, Tooling, Simulation, Program Management, suppliers, and OEM customers throughout equipment design, buy-off, installation, commissioning, and production support.




Key Responsibilities

Manufacturing & Robotics Engineering

Design and develop robotic welding and automated assembly processes for automotive ladder frames, subframes, cradles, and chassis assemblies.Define robotic cell layouts, process flow, tooling concepts, and equipment specifications.Lead robotic cell design reviews, feasibility studies, and manufacturing readiness assessments.Optimize cycle time, robot utilization, line balancing, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE).Develop equipment standards to support global manufacturing consistency.


Robotic Welding & Automation

Program and optimize industrial robots including FANUC, ABB, KUKA. Preferably KUKADevelop robotic welding paths for MIG, MAG, resistance spot welding, projection welding, and laser welding applications.Optimize weld schedules, robot motions, weld quality, and consumable utilization.Support robotic vision systems, weld inspection, seam tracking, and adaptive welding technologies.Troubleshoot robotic equipment, weld defects, and automation issues during launch and production.

description:
AI & Marketing Technology Specialist

SUPPLY | Independent Media Agency

Location: Boulder/Denver preferred | Remote within Mountain Time consideredEmployment: Full-timeSalary: $75,000–$100,000 annually

Curious minds wanted. Especially the ones who like building things.There's a good chance you've already found a dozen ways AI can make your work easier. You've experimented with new tools, connected systems, built something useful, or taught yourself a technology simply because you wanted to see what it could do.

You probably have a running list of things you think could be done better.

If this sounds like you, keep reading.

SUPPLY is looking for an AI & Marketing Technology Specialist to help us discover, build, and implement smarter ways of working across our agency, while exploring new technology-driven opportunities for our clients.

You'll work directly with agency leadership and collaborate across media, strategy, analytics, and account teams. Your initial focus will be improving how our agency operates, using AI, automation, integrations, and other technologies to solve real problems.

You'll also have opportunities to prototype new capabilities, experiment with emerging media technologies, and help bring innovative client ideas to life.

This isn't a role where you'll be confined to maintaining one dashboard or supporting one platform. You'll encounter different challenges, learn new technologies, recommend solutions, and help build things that didn't exist before.

We're looking for someone who can turn curiosity into something useful.

More Than Automation: Help Build What's NextWe're building a more intentional approach to innovation at SUPPLY, connecting ideas from media, data, audience intelligence, creative technology, and AI.

Some opportunities will involve making our internal operations more efficient. Others will focus on developing capabilities that help our teams and clients make better decisions, reach audiences in new ways, or explore what's possible with emerging technology.

You won't be expected to know every technology or solve every challenge independently. You'll collaborate with experienced media, strategy, and analytics professionals who understand the business, while contributing technical curiosity, problem-solving, and hands-on execution.

The goal isn't to chase every new technology. It's to identify what's genuinely useful, build something that works, and help turn the best ideas into lasting capabilities.

A Few Examples of What You Might Help BuildThese are examples of opportunities we're interested in exploring, not a fixed project list:

Workflow Automation: Build AI-enabled workflows, integrations, and tools that reduce repetitive work, improve collaboration, and give our teams more time for higher-value thinking.Media Intelligence Tools: Connect campaign performance, audience insights, market data, and business outcomes to help teams make smarter media decisions.AI-Powered Audience Intelligence: Develop ways to analyze audience behaviors, uncover meaningful differences between customer segments, and translate findings into marketing opportunities.Creative Testing Capabilities: Explore how AI and technology can help evaluate messaging, creative variations, and media approaches more efficiently.Interactive Media Experiences: Prototype new ways for consumers to engage with brands through technology, interactive advertising, and emerging media platforms.We don't expect one person to build all of these independently. We're looking for someone excited about helping turn possibilities like these into working solutions.

A Little About SUPPLYSUPPLY is an independent media agency headquartered in Boulder, Colorado.

We help ambitious brands navigate an increasingly complex media landscape through strategy, media planning and buying, analytics, and technology.

Our work spans traditional and digital media, including television, streaming, programmatic, social, search, and emerging channels.

We're independent by design. We value good thinking over unnecessary process, collaboration over silos, and people who take ownership of their work.

We believe there are enormous opportunities for people who can recognize where technology makes a difference and turn good ideas into practical improvements.

What You'll DoMake SUPPLY work betterIdentify manual, repetitive, or inefficient processes and develop better ways to handle them.Build and implement automations, AI-enabled workflows, and integrations that improve internal operations.Explore opportunities to help teams collaborate, share information, and accomplish work more effectively.Work with colleagues to understand problems, develop solutions, and help people adopt them.Explore and apply emerging technologyResearch, experiment with, and evaluate AI tools, automation platforms, and emerging technologies.Identify technologies with genuine business potential and recommend practical applications.Build prototypes, test ideas, learn from the results, and help implement promising solutions.Help develop new capabilities through SUPPLY's innovation initiatives, working with agency teams to turn ideas into practical applications.Stay curious about how technology is changing the media and advertising industry.Improve our data and technology capabilitiesHelp improve how data moves between systems, platforms, and teams.Develop or enhance reporting workflows, dashboards, campaign tracking, and measurement capabilities.Support integrations between media platforms, analytics systems, and internal tools.Help make information more accessible, actionable, and useful.Turn problems into working solutionsTranslate business challenges into clear technical next steps.Prioritize opportunities based on impact, feasibility, effort, and usefulness.Build with an understanding of data privacy, security, and responsible AI use.Communicate progress, document solutions, and help colleagues understand and use what you've developed.Take ownership of projects from the initial idea through implementation and improvement.What We're Looking ForWe're open to candidates from different educational and professional backgrounds. You might have studied computer science, data analytics, marketing, information systems, engineering, or something entirely different.

This role is particularly well suited to someone with approximately 0–4 years of relevant professional experience, although demonstrated capability matters more than a specific number of years.

What matters most:

Genuine curiosity about AI, automation, and emerging technology.Demonstrated experience building, automating, integrating, or improving something using technology.The ability to independently learn new tools and technical concepts.Strong analytical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills.Comfort working across different technologies and business challenges.Good judgment about what to prioritize and when a simpler solution is better.Initiative, ownership, and the ability to move from ideas to execution.Clear communication skills and an ability to work with colleagues who aren't technical specialists.A willingness to test ideas, learn from mistakes, and improve solutions based on feedback.You don't need to know every platform or programming language. You do need evidence that you can figure things out and build something useful.

Experience That Would Catch Our AttentionThese are examples, not a checklist. You don't need experience with every tool or technology listed.

Building automations using Zapier, Make, n8n, or similar platforms.Creating AI workflows, agents, or applications using large language models.Working with APIs, webhooks, and integrations.Writing code in Python, JavaScript, SQL, or similar languages.Using AI-assisted development tools to build applications or solve technical problems.Working with marketing data, analytics platforms, or reporting systems.Creating dashboards, internal applications, or tools that help others work more effectively.Experimenting with databases, cloud applications, or connected systems.Identifying and solving a problem nobody specifically assigned you.Personal projects count. Side projects count. Things you've built because you were curious absolutely count.

We care more about what you can learn, build, and improve than how many software logos appear on your résumé.

You'll Probably Enjoy Working Here If...You hear about a new AI capability and immediately want to figure out what you could do with it.You've automated something that technically only took five minutes because you knew you'd have to do it 500 more times.You like understanding how systems work and figuring out how they could work better.You enjoy working through unfamiliar problems without needing every step prescribed.You're willing to recommend an approach, test it, and change direction when something isn't working.You find satisfaction in building something other people actually use.You're comfortable balancing experimentation with deadlines and practical business needs.You enjoy collaborating with people who bring different expertise to the table.What Makes This Opportunity DifferentTechnology isn't an isolated IT function at SUPPLY. It's increasingly central to how we work, what we can build, and how we create value for clients.

You'll have exposure to agency operations, media technology, analytics, audience intelligence, and client-facing innovation.

You'll work closely with experienced colleagues and agency leadership, with the opportunity to help shape new capabilities rather than simply maintain existing systems.

It's a role with meaningful responsibility, room to experiment, and plenty of opportunity to learn and grow.

Location & FlexibilitySUPPLY is headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, and we operate in a flexible, remote-friendly environment.

We'd especially welcome candidates in the Boulder/Denver area who can collaborate with our team in person periodically. We're also open to strong candidates elsewhere in Mountain Time.

We believe flexibility and collaboration can coexist, and we value opportunities to work together in person when they're useful.

description:
The goal of a Machine Learning Engineer at Scale is to leverage techniques in the fields of generative AI, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and agentic AI to improve Scale's products and customer experience in production environments. Our machine learning engineers take advantage of robust internal infrastructure and unique access to massive datasets to deliver improvements to our customers.


Our Public Sector Machine Learning team is focused on deploying cutting-edge models to mission-critical government systems through products like and. Our work spans multiple modalities, with a strong focus on both large language models and computer vision. On the LLM side, we are developing agentic systems that help solve complex operational and planning challenges for government partners. This includes building agent frameworks that integrate with custom retrieval pipelines and production APIs, as well as evaluation tools to benchmark and refine agent behavior. We're also advancing research in areas like reinforcement learning for agentic LLMs, with successful deployment into real-world operational environments. On the computer vision front, we're training advanced models to increase labeling throughput and automate perception tasks. Our efforts include building large-scale fine-tuning pipelines, training models across multiple modalities, and developing generalizable vision foundation models to support a wide range of defense applications.


You will:

Take state of the art models developed internally and from the community, use them in production to solve problems for our customers and taskers
Improve and maintain production models through retraining, hyperparameter tuning, and architectural updates, while preserving core performance characteristics
Collaborate with product and research teams to identify and prototype ML-driven product enhancements, including for upcoming product lines
Work with massive datasets to develop both generic models as well as fine tune models for specific products
Build scalable machine learning infrastructure to automate and optimize our ML services
Serve as a cross-functional representative and advocate for machine learning techniques across engineering and product organizations
Be comfortable learning new technologies quickly and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
Comfortable with light travel (approximately 10%) for customer interaction and team needs

This role will require an active TS security clearance


Ideally You'd Have:

2+yearsof experience building and deploying applied ML systems in production environments
Extensive experience with GenAI, Agentic AI, natural language processing, deep learning and deep reinforcement learning, or computer vision in a production environment
Solid background in algorithms, data structures, and object-oriented programming
Strong programming skills in Python, experience in Tensorflow or PyTorch

Nice to Haves:

Experience deploying software into environments you can't reach from your laptop - on-prem, edge, air-gapped, or otherwise restricted networks. Regulated industries count; the constraint is the point, not the sector.
Any prior exposure to government or defense work: military or civilian service, a cleared internship, or time at a federal contractor.
Hands-on fine-tuning of open-weight models - LoRA/PEFT, instruction tuning, or training embedding models, at work or on your own.
Having written evaluations for a system whose output isn't deterministic: benchmarks, LLM judges, or a regression suite that caught something real.
Experience with geospatial data or maps - GIS tooling, spatial reference systems, or imagery.
A shipped project with real users behind it, where you owned it after launch rather than handing it off at merge.

description:
SEL is looking for a people-oriented Mechanical/Robotics Engineer to join our Product Support and Development - Mechanical team in our Manufacturing Division. Our team develops and integrates mechanical and robotic solutions for our manufacturing facilities that enable us to build our products in a safer, more reliable, or more economical way.


 

 As an engineer in this role, day-to-day is a mix of hands-on design work, problem-solving, and working directly with your customers. You'll own everything from problem statement creation to solution integration and closing out the projects. You'll primarily be focused on leading a small team to develop automation solutions that make our production environments safer, more reliable, and more economical. You'll use tools like collaborative/industrial robotics, end-of-arm tooling, computer vision tools, and self-developed mechanical tools/fixtures. CAD work is a regular thing, whether you're building new designs or tweaking existing ones.


 

 Your solutions will be brought to life on the production floor so making sure they actually work in the real world is huge. Design quality and collaboration are a big part of our day, so expect to be involved in design reviews and giving feedback. While you lead projects and your small team, you'll be focused on delivering results on time and within budget while also developing employees as they progress in their careers.


 

 Required Qualifications:


 
 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Manufacturing Engineering
 Approximately 2+ years of experience in three or more of the following areas: 
 
 Automation integration
 Materials and processes
 Mechanics
 CAD
 Manufacturing engineering
 Electronic manufacturing techniques
 
 
 
 Strong problem-solving skills
 Ability to manage and track projects effectively
 Clear and effective communication skills—written, verbal, and documentation
 Quick to learn new skills and open to taking on new responsibilities
 Works well in team environments
 Must pass a background check and drug test per SEL requirements
 
 

 Preferred Qualifications:


 We're looking for someone who has led small teams and knows how to keep things moving. If you've worked with robotics, especially Universal Robots Cobots, and vision systems, that's a big plus. Experience supporting design, automation, or general engineering in a manufacturing setting is highly valuable. And if you've written or run Design of Experiments before, even better.


 

 Location(s): (Will work from both locations, about 45 min apart)


 
 Lewiston, ID – This position is located in Lewiston, ID where you'll enjoy an unmatched quality of life. Enjoy the smaller town life: country space, freedom from traffic, easy access to recreational activities in nearby mountains, rivers, and forests, as well as great schools and universities.
 Pullman, WA – This position is located in Pullman, WA. Nestled in Eastern Washington, offering an exceptional quality of life. Embrace the charm of small-town living with spacious surroundings, no traffic hassles, and easy access to outdoor adventures in nearby mountains, rivers, and forests. Plus, benefit from excellent schools and universities in the area.
 
 


 Competitive pay. Superior benefits. Inspiring work. 


 People are at the core of our company and we hire employee-owners. We welcome you to learn more about how we support employees.


 
 We're 100% employee owned. Retirement benefits include an employer funded stock ownership plan (ESOP) and personal 401(k) options.
 We offer top tier medical, prescription, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance.
 We recognize the importance of a healthy life balance and offer: 10 paid holidays, annual vacation accrual starting at 12 days, 9 paid sick days, and paid family and medical leave that covers 90% of your pay.
 We foster growth and development of our employees through avenues such as STEM courses, apprenticeships, tuition assistance, and engineering development programs.
 Ask our team about other benefits including wellness, fertility, adoption, and flexible spending benefits.
 
 


 Pay Range Information: $102,900 - $130,000 per year


 The range for this role is $102,900 - $130,000 annually. We set starting pay based on job-related factors such as your experience, training, knowledge, and skills. We are looking to fill this position at the Mechanical Engineer level, and we welcome applicants with a range of experience. Depending on your background, we may consider you for a different level, with compensation aligned accordingly.


 


 Communication with Applicants


 We communicate with all applicants. If you do not receive a response about your application, please check your SPAM filter or reach out to us at careers@selinc.com.


 


 SEL is an Equal Opportunity Employer: Vets/Disabled.

description:
Why Shuttlebase?Every day, millions of people decide whether to buy something online, and the reasons behind those decisions are still mostly guesswork. We want to change that. 

We're working to quantify human psychology: to build an embedding model for human behavior that understands how people react to a page, a price, or a single sentence, and can predict what will work before anyone runs a test.

Every experiment our AI runs on a live store teaches that model something about how people decide. Our goal is for any company to be able to ask, "I'm selling product X to audience Y, how do I optimize for Z?" and get an answer it can trust.

We're early and well funded. The people who join now will pick the tools, design the models, and help choose who joins next. If that's a problem you want to spend the next few years on, we'd like to meet you.



Applied Scientist, Behavior ModelingEvery day our script records tens of millions of actions from people visiting the websites we work with: what they look at, where they hesitate, what they click, and when they leave. You'll turn that into the first version of our behavior model. The goal is a model that predicts how people are likely to interact with a website, and what the site should and shouldn't do for them. 

We'll start with online stores, since that's where we work today, by spotting which visitors are close to buying and which groups need to see a different version of the page. Researchers have published a lot about learning from user behavior with sequence models and embeddings, so you won't start from a blank page. Your job is to know that work well, pick what fits our data, get it working here, and keep up as the field moves. 

You'd be the first person working on this full time, so a lot rests on your shoulders!



What you'll work onThe behavior model. Build our first model that turns raw session events into embeddings of how a visitor behaves. Pre-training a transformer on event sequences is a likely start, but you'll make the call. The hard part is that most sessions are short and anonymous, and most visitors never come back.

Buying intent and audiences. Use the model to spot buying intent during a session and to group visitors into audiences, so the AI can show each audience the page version that works for it. We want a first version on live stores as soon as it works, and we'll improve it from there.

New research. When a paper comes out that could help, you'll be the one who reads it, tries it on our data, and decides whether we use it. If you learn something worth publishing, publish it.

We mostly work in Python, with event data in ClickHouse and services on AWS. You'll report directly to our CTO, and work every day with our engineers, who build on your model, and with our client team, who explain to stores why the AI showed their shoppers a different page. A lot of what they say will come from you.



You'll love this job ifYou read papers and get impatient until you've tried the idea on real data.

You'd rather adapt a proven method and see it work in three weeks than spend a year inventing a new one.

You want a big, open problem that's yours to figure out, with engineers and the founders working right next to you.

You're fine working with noisy event logs and writing your own SQL to get at them.

You were the person in your lab others came to when they needed a hard idea made simple.

You want to help build a model that understands how people make decisions, and you'd like to be there for the first version of it.



What you bringA PhD or equivalent research experience in a quantitative field. People from physics, math, computational biology, and neuroscience often fit well, especially if you've modeled behavior or sequences.

You've trained a model on messy, real-world sequence or time-series data yourself, and you've shown whether it worked.

You know the recent work on learning from sequences (transformers, self-supervised pre-training, embeddings) well enough to choose between approaches and explain why.

You write solid Python and can pull your own data with SQL.

You've given talks or written for people outside your field, and they followed.

Bonus: experience with recommendation systems or user behavior data, large event datasets, or eCommerce.



What We ValueCuriosity and excellence: We're trying to understand why people decide what they do, so asking questions is the job. We push on each other's ideas, and a failed experiment teaches us as much as a winning one.

Whatever it takes: If something needs doing, whoever can do it does it, whatever their title. Our clients' results are our results.

Ownership: Shipping something is where the work starts. You follow it all the way to the result, and when you get something wrong, you say so and fix it. We keep our promises, the big ones and the small ones.

Agility: Most ideas go from whiteboard to working prototype in two or three days. If something isn't working, we drop it fast, and nobody holds it against you.

Enjoy the ride: Building something new comes with rough weeks. We get through them together and celebrate the good ones.



What We OfferCompetitive compensation

Meaningful equity - real ownership in Shuttlebase's success.

Medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family.

Unlimited PTO - we trust you to take the time you need.

Tax free commuter and parking benefits

Office-first culture (4 days/week) - Midtown Manhattan, in the middle of it all.

Work directly with the founding team - your impact is immediate, visible, and career-defining.

Free One Medical Membership

401k

Six Feet Up is seeking a Senior Data Engineer with deep experience designing, building, and maintaining secure, scalable data systems.


 In this role, you will work with cross-functional teams to turn complex data challenges into reliable production solutions. You will design data pipelines, build processing workflows, improve data quality, support machine learning initiatives, and help clients make better use of structured, unstructured, time-series, sensor-based, and high-volume data.


 We are looking for someone who can bring technical leadership, sound engineering judgment, and strong communication skills to ambiguous data problems. The ideal candidate is comfortable working across data engineering, cloud infrastructure, machine learning support, and production software delivery.


 What You'll Do
 As a Senior Data Engineer, you will:


 
 Design, build, and maintain robust, scalable data pipelines
 Develop ETL/ELT workflows for collecting, transforming, validating, and storing data
 Work with cloud-based data processing and storage systems
 Implement data validation, quality checks, monitoring, and transformation workflows
 Process complex datasets, including noisy, high-volume, time-series, sensor, or device-generated data
 Support machine learning workflows, including data preparation, model training, evaluation, and production integration
 Collaborate with data scientists, researchers, software engineers, and client stakeholders
 Translate prototype data workflows into reliable, maintainable production systems
 Create systems that are well-documented, testable, secure, and ready for audit or review
 Communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
 
 Your Technical Expertise
 We are looking for someone with strong hands-on experience in:


 
 Data pipeline architecture and implementation
 ETL/ELT orchestration tools such as Airflow, Dagster, or similar platforms
 Python-based data engineering and data processing tools
 Cloud-based data infrastructure, storage, and processing
 Data modeling, schema design, validation, and quality-control practices
 Working with public, proprietary, structured, and unstructured datasets
 Time-series, sensor, IoT, or other high-volume data sources
 Supporting machine learning or data science teams with reliable data workflows
 Building reproducible, testable, and maintainable data systems
 Version control, automated testing, and collaborative software development practices
 
 Strong Candidates May Also Have Experience With
 
 Machine learning pipelines for classification, prediction, recommendation, or categorization systems
 MLOps, model evaluation, experiment tracking, and reproducible ML workflows
 Processing noisy signal data or other data that requires cleaning, filtering, or feature extraction
 Healthcare, digital health, research, or regulated software environments
 HIPAA, privacy-preserving data architecture, or secure cloud data processing
 Working with sensitive, clinical, or user-generated data
 Helping researchers or domain experts scale early-stage algorithms into production-ready systems
 Designing systems that support thousands or more users
 
 A Plus: 


 
 Experience with containers, CI/CD, DevOps practices, or Kubernetes
 Familiarity with AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or similar cloud platforms
 Experience with consumer analytics, dashboards, or data visualization products
 Experience supporting FDA, SaMD, clinical validation, audit, or regulatory documentation efforts
 Experience designing secure data workflows for privacy-sensitive applications
 
 About You
 You are a senior engineer who brings structure to ambiguous technical challenges. You ask thoughtful questions, identify risks early, and know how to balance research needs, business goals, engineering quality, and long-term maintainability.


 You care about data quality, privacy, testing, documentation, and clear communication. You are comfortable designing architecture, writing production code, reviewing data workflows, and collaborating with people from different technical backgrounds.


 You enjoy helping clients move from ideas and prototypes to secure, scalable, production-ready systems.


 If you are a motivated Senior Data Engineer seeking a challenging and meaningful role, we encourage you to apply.


 About Six Feet Up
 Six Feet Up makes the world a better place by using technology to accelerate the initiatives of companies that do good. Our engineers specialize in app development, AI, big data and cloud technology. Our impactful clients focus on tech & science, social good, and the environment.

STRI provides a global platform for research on tropical forests and marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and human well-being.

The ForestGEO program is a global network of scientists and forest research sites dedicated to advancing the long-term study of the world's forests. 

The GEO-TREES initiative builds on this network to improve the accuracy and verification of global forest carbon estimates through collaboration among forest research sites worldwide. The Data Scientist supports the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO) and GEO-TREES programs as a liaison between site-based data collection and the development of analytical data products.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIESData Management, Scientific Analysis, and Software Programming (50%)
Performs data-management, computational, and bioinformatics assignments supporting research in tropical biology, ecology, and forestry.
Develops, implements, modifies, and maintains data-processing pipelines used to process plot-based tree inventory and related ecological data and to derive estimates such as forest woody biomass density.
Evaluates the performance of existing data-processing pipelines and recommends modifications or improvements based on data characteristics, analytical requirements, user needs, and experience working with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES site teams.
Develops and modifies computational procedures for analysis of ForestGEO and GEO-TREES scientific data using established data-science principles, methods, and practices.
Processes, validates, organizes, and manages tree inventory, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS), and Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) data for scientific analysis and long-term storage.
Supports the archiving and long-term management of scientific datasets to ensure appropriate organization, documentation, accessibility, and usability.
Develops and maintains data-management solutions and informatics workflows for data acquisition, formatting, validation, processing, analysis, use, and storage.
Implements established data standards and contributes to the development and modification of data structures and architectures appropriate to assigned projects.
Writes, tests, documents, troubleshoots, and maintains computer code used in data-processing and analytical workflows.
Uses programming languages and tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, GIS applications, and related scientific and data-management software.
Identifies data-quality problems, inconsistencies, missing values, formatting issues, and other anomalies and determines appropriate methods for correcting or documenting them.
Works with researchers and other technical personnel to ensure that processed data and analyticalproducts meet established scientific and program requirements.


Requirements Gathering and Technical Support (25%)

Works closely with researchers and program personnel to identify data-processing, analytical, software, and data-management requirements for assigned scientific projects.
Conducts technical analyses of available methods and alternatives and recommends appropriate software tools, workflows, calculations, and analytical approaches.
Assists researchers in translating scientific requirements into practical data-processing and
computational solutions.
Evaluates existing workflows and recommends modifications when established approaches do not fully address the characteristics of the data or requirements of an assigned project.
Coordinates with site representatives concerning timelines and technical requirements for acquisition and submission of plot inventory, TLS, ALS, GNSS, and related scientific data.
Reviews submitted data to determine whether established ForestGEO and GEO-TREES formatting, documentation, and data-quality requirements have been met.
Works with site personnel to resolve routine and moderately complex data-submission and data-quality problems.
Coordinates with the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) and other appropriate technical staff to ensure assigned development activities follow applicable systems-development, documentation, version-control, security, and software-development practices.
Prepares technical documentation describing data-processing workflows, code, data structures, analytical procedures, and related methods.
Assists in testing new or modified software tools, workflows, and procedures prior to implementation.


Training and Collaboration (25%)

Develops and provides formal and informal training to researchers, site personnel, and program partners concerning ForestGEO and GEO-TREES data systems, data-management procedures, formatting requirements, data-processing workflows, and related tools.
Serves as a technical point of contact for tree-inventory teams and other users at assigned ForestGEO and GEO-TREES sites.
Provides advice, training, troubleshooting assistance, and technical support concerning data collection, formatting, cleaning, validation, processing, documentation, and submission.
Explains data standards, analytical procedures, software requirements, and data-management practices to researchers and partners with varying levels of technical expertise.
Collaborates with scientists, data managers, programmers, and other personnel to identify and resolve data-management and processing problems.
Participates in meetings, working groups, and collaborative activities involving ForestGEO, GEO-TREES, Smithsonian staff, and domestic and international research partners.
Shares information concerning lessons learned, recurring data problems, workflow improvements, and effective data-management practices with program staff and partners.
Performs other duties as assigned.
QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTSEducation and Experience:
Professional knowledge of and skill in applying a wide range of data-science principles, concepts, methods, and practices sufficient to perform difficult data-management, processing, computational, and analytical assignments involving ecological and forestry data.
Knowledge of data acquisition, data cleaning, validation, transformation, integration, storage, analysis, visualization, documentation, and reproducible computational workflows.
Knowledge of computational and data-management methods is required to develop, modify, implement, and maintain processing pipelines for tree inventory, GNSS, ALS, TLS, spatial, and related scientific datasets.
Knowledge of programming concepts and skill in applying programming languages and analytical tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, and related software to manipulate, process, analyze, and manage scientific data.
Knowledge of algorithm development, software testing, version control, debugging, documentation, deployment, and maintenance practices is required to support scientific applications and data-processing workflows.
Knowledge of spatial-data concepts, common spatial-data formats, and GIS software is required to process and evaluate geospatial information associated with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES projects.
Knowledge of the scientific concepts associated with ecology, tropical biology, forestry, or related environmental sciences sufficient to understand data characteristics, research requirements, analytical objectives, and the relationships among data variables.
Knowledge to select and modify appropriate data-processing and analytical methods; identify and resolve data-quality problems; evaluate alternative computational approaches; interpret results; develop recommendations; and prepare technical documentation and analytical products.
Skill adapting or modifying established data-science techniques and procedures to address differences in data structure, quality, collection methods, analytical requirements, or site-specific circumstances.

description:
About the Role
This is a rare chance to learn data science from the inside out at one of the fastest-growing healthcare startups in the country. As an Associate Data Scientist at Solace, you'll work on the forecasting and machine learning systems that operate our marketplace in real time: matching patients with advocates, predicting demand, and keeping the business ahead of its own growth.


You won't spend your first year re-deriving textbook exercises. You'll contribute to real models with mentorship from senior data scientists, and you'll be expected to think independently, question your own results, and defend your methodology. You don't need years of experience, but you do need an innate ability to get things done.


This role is for the ambitious, the curious, and those who don't shy away from feedback. If you're the kind of person who sees a problem and can't resist solving it, keep reading.


This is an in person role in our Redwood City office, 3 days a week.


What You'll Do
Contribute to real predictive models in your first weeks: forecasting, matching, and scoring systems that the business runs on.


Pull and wrangle your own data with SQL from Snowflake. Nobody hands you a clean CSV here.


Support the design and analysis of A/B tests and experiments, learning how to measure the true impact of product and operational changes.


Work alongside data engineers to see how models get from a notebook into production, learning MLOps practices as you go.


Apply statistics with rigor: knowing when a result is real, when it's noise, and how to tell the difference.


Present your findings and defend your methodology to technical and non-technical audiences. Your voice matters here, even on day one.


Grow your craft: learn how to frame problems, validate models, design experiments, and make smart modeling decisions.


What You Bring to the Table
A bachelor's or master's degree in Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science, Applied Math, or a related quantitative field (or equivalent practical experience), graduating between December 2026 and June 2027.


Strong fundamentals in statistics and probability: hypothesis testing, regression, and the judgment to know when your model is fooling you.


Working Python skills, including the core data science ecosystem (pandas, scikit-learn, NumPy), plus working SQL.


Projects that show you can do real quantitative work: research, internships, Kaggle competitions, hackathons, or personal modeling projects. We care about what you've built and what you learned from it, not just what you studied.


A bias toward action. You have an exceptional craving for momentum, and you'd rather ship a simple model that works than polish a complex one that never launches.


Curiosity for how systems work, comfort with ambiguity, and a refined palate for controlled chaos.


Confident communication. You can explain a model to someone who has never heard of one, and take critique of your methodology without defensiveness.


A sense of care. You take pride in the details, because in healthcare data, the details are the difference.


A hunger to learn and an ego small enough to admit when you don't know something.


Bonus Points
Exposure to time-series forecasting (ARIMA, Prophet, exponential smoothing).


Coursework or projects in causal inference or experimental design.


Familiarity with dbt, Airflow, Docker, or cloud environments (AWS).


Experience with NLP or unstructured text data.


Up for the Challenge?
We look forward to meeting you.

Senior Cloud Automation Engineer – GCP & AI

Location: Chicago, IL

Focus: Cloud Infrastructure | Python | Java | Automation | AI

W2 Only: $60.00 per hour; we cannot work C2C 

No Sponsorship or visa transfer available

6 -month contract that will be extended based on performance




Our client is seeking a hands-on Cloud Automation Engineer to help modernize and automate complex technology operations within a large-scale, high-availability environment.

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys solving technical challenges, writing code, and finding creative ways to eliminate manual work. You'll work with cloud infrastructure, automation tools, and emerging AI technologies to improve how systems are monitored, managed, and supported.

A key focus will be leveraging agentic AI and automation to simplify operational processes, develop intelligent dashboards, and improve efficiency across critical platforms.




What You'll Be Working On

Develop Python-based automation tools and scripts to streamline infrastructure and operational processes.Build and enhance automated dashboards that provide visibility into system performance and operations.Explore opportunities to leverage agentic AI, including Google Gemini and related technologies, to automate complex operational tasks.Support cloud infrastructure automation within Google Cloud Platform (GCP).Develop and maintain Infrastructure as Code (IaC) solutions.Work with CI/CD pipelines to improve deployment and operational workflows.Identify repetitive or manual processes and create scalable automation solutions.Work with compute infrastructure and cloud services to improve platform efficiency and reliability.Collaborate with engineering and operations teams supporting business-critical, 24/7 platforms.Troubleshoot technical challenges and contribute to ongoing infrastructure improvements.


What We're Looking For

Strong hands-on Python development experience, including coding, scripting, and automation.Java development experience, ideally 2–3 years.Approximately 2–3 years of Python development experience.Practical experience working with Google Cloud Platform (GCP).Experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC), preferably Terraform.Understanding of cloud compute infrastructure and how different components work together.Experience with CI/CD pipelines and automated deployment processes.Ability to write, troubleshoot, and maintain production-quality code.Strong problem-solving skills and an interest in improving operational processes through automation.Ability to work effectively in an environment supporting highly available, business-critical systems.


Nice to Have

Experience with agentic AI, Google Gemini, or other AI-powered development tools.Exposure to AI-driven operations, intelligent dashboards, or automated remediation.Experience with Terraform and Terragrunt.Background supporting large-scale cloud infrastructure or 24/7 technology platforms.Familiarity with Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) or DevOps practices.


What Makes This Opportunity Interesting

This isn't a traditional SRE position focused primarily on monitoring and incident response. You'll have the opportunity to build solutions that change how infrastructure operations are managed, using a combination of software engineering, cloud technologies, and AI-driven automation.

We're looking for someone who enjoys both keeping complex systems running and developing better ways to operate them.

description:
Join the Clean Energy Revolution

 

Become a Data Engineering Advisor at Southern California Edison (SCE) and build a better tomorrow. In this job, you'll serve as a strategic technical leader responsible for enabling Grid modernization, operational intelligence, data-driven decision making and AI adoption across SCE. Your objective is to drive adoption of the Grid Data Platform while guiding its continuous improvement and evolution to meet SCE's changing business and technology needs.

 

As a Data Engineering Advisor, your work will help power our planet, reduce carbon emissions and create cleaner air for everyone. Are you ready to take on the challenge to help us build the future?

 

Responsibilities Manages and scales data pipelines from internal and external data sources to support new product launches and drive data quality across data products.Facilitates data engineering activities covering data acquisition, extraction, normalization, transformation, management, and manipulation of large and complex data sets.Keeps abreast of new and current data engineering, big data and data science techniques. Researches methods, techniques, and new practices; develops and promotes data engineering best practices, standards and guidelines.Works closely with subject matter experts to design and develop front-end applications with data models and data pipelines supporting the applications.Provides governance and oversight of data assets, data environments and relevant data procedures, with the proactive planning and enforcement of data asset naming conventions.Builds and maintains data pipelines using big data processing technologies to process and analyze large datasets; uses ETL processes on the internal cluster.Develops and maintains data warehouse schema and data models, ensuring data consistency and accuracy.Ensures ongoing alignment of technical and business strategies based on changing business and technology drivers and risks.Creates advanced visualizations and tools to provide insight, drives action, and supports work throughout the business.Identifies and designs Data-as-a-Service candidates for improved data availability and consumption.A material job duty of all positions within the Company is ensuring the protection of all its physical, financial and cybersecurity assets, and properly accessing and managing private customer data, proprietary information, confidential medical records, and other types of highly sensitive information and data with the highest standards of conduct and integrity.Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Statistics/ Mathematics or equivalent STEM major.Seven or more years of experience in data processing large data sets, hands-on with data transformation, aggregation, and filtering. 

Preferred Qualifications

 

Seven or more years of experience designing, implementing, and supporting enterprise-scale data platforms, data lakes, lakehouses, data fabrics, or modern analytics ecosystems.Experience leading the architecture, engineering, and operationalization of large-scale data platforms supporting utility, energy, critical infrastructure, or operational technology (OT) environments.Experience establishing DataOps, DevSecOps, and CI/CD practices for data engineering teamsKnowledge of utility regulatory, cybersecurity, and compliance requirements, including NERC-CIP, data privacy, and critical infrastructure protection principles.Experience serving as a technical leader for cross-functional initiatives involving Grid Operations, Asset Management, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and enterprise data organizations. 

Additional Information 

 

This position's work mode is hybrid. The employee will report to an SCE facility for a set number of days with the option to work remotely on the remaining days. Unless otherwise noted, employees are required to work and reside in the state of California. Further details of this work mode will be discussed at the interview stage. The work mode can be changed based on business needs.Visit our Candidate Resource page to get meaningful information related to benefits, perks, resources, testing information, hiring process, and more!Qualified applications with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act.The primary work location for this position is Rosemead, CA. Position will require up to 20% traveling and being out in the field throughout the SCE service territory. This position has been identified as a NERC/CIP impacted position - Prior to being hired, the successful candidate must pass a Personnel Risk Assessment (PRA) or Background Investigation. Once hired, the candidate must complete specified training prior to gaining un-escorted access to assigned work location and performing necessary job duties. 

About Southern California Edison

 

The people at SCE don't just keep the lights on. Our mission is so much bigger. We're fueling the kind of innovation that's changing an entire industry, and quite possibly the planet. Join us and create a future with cleaner energy, while providing our customers with the safety and reliability they demand. At SCE, you'll have a chance to grow personally and professionally, making a real impact in Southern California and around the world.

 

Southern California Edison is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status.

 

We are committed to ensuring that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodations at AskHR@sce.com or (626) 302-3456 and select option 2.

description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. SOFTWARE ENGINEER, COMPUTER VISION


We are looking for exceptional, driven, adaptable, and resilient senior software engineers who are technical leaders and experts in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and computer vision. As a software engineer on the NDE & Materials Software team, you will accelerate the quality, speed, and efficiency of manufacturing processes at SpaceX by owning end-to-end solutions - from model development to production deployment and monitoring.


Our team is building the next generation of in-process monitoring tools for SpaceX as we develop the Starship, Raptor, and Starlink programs. We deliver high-impact solutions through advanced AI models and scalable simulation with a focus on non-destructive evaluation (NDE) and materials engineering applications. As a technical leader, you will guide the team in applying cutting-edge AI to these manufacturing challenges.


RESPONSIBILITIES:



Lead computer vision model development and deployment for real-time inspection and automated defect recognition in production-scale manufacturing
Architect and implement pipelines for scalable model training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and retraining using industry-standard tools like Ray Train/Serve, Kubeflow, Airflow, or equivalent
Develop software to integrate hardware, sensors, and tooling (including sensor fusion) with AI-driven process monitoring systems
Build and optimize data pipelines from production lines, incorporating real-time stream processing and inference
Collaborate with part/process engineers, NDE engineers, and materials scientists to link advanced models and outputs to manufacturing
Lead design and code reviews, technology evaluations, and enforce best practices (e.g., style, CI/CD, accuracy, testability, efficiency, and standards)

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:



Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, physics, or related STEM discipline; OR 8+ years of professional experience building and deploying AI software/Machine Learning in lieu of a degree
5+ years of software development experience
3+ years deploying AI models to production environments
3+ years of software engineering experience
3+ years of experience leveraging Python for data analysis

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:



Proven track record as a technical leader in software projects involving AI/ML
Hands-on experience deploying computer vision models for real-time manufacturing inspection and defect detection
Strong development experience in Python and C++ (or similar), with expertise in ML frameworks like PyTorch or JAX
Hands-on experience with computer vision libraries (e.g., OpenCV)Experience fine tuning and adapting state-of-the-art models, such as transformers and vision transformers, to production environments
Experience fine-tuning LLMs or vision-language models and building agentic tools
Experience deploying applications at scale with Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud/edge inference for factory automation
Expertise in machine learning/LLM operations including model versioning, A/B testing, drift detection, and orchestration with Kubeflow, Ray, MLFlow, or similar
Stream processing with Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, or equivalent
Database expertise in PostgreSQL or similar and data tools (Prometheus, Grafana, Jupyter)
Strong linux experience
Experience applying AI to physics or simulation domains, using physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) or surrogate modeling

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:



Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary
Ability to travel to other SpaceX sites as needed (up to 20%)

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS: 


Pay range: 
Sr. Software Engineer: $160,000.00 - $225,000.00/per year 
 
Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.


Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:



To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. description:
We are looking for a Data Analytics Manager to work with our Podcasts, Creator Payouts, and Ads Revenue data team. Your mission will be to support the data operations for enterprise and individual podcast creator calculations, perform analytics over advertising revenue, and manage a team to provide insights to both internal and external stakeholders within Accounting, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), and the broader Finance organization.
What You'll Do
Manage a team of data scientists and work with large data sets, solving complex problems in a dynamic environment
Work with our Engineers to support the development of systems, datasets, and processes to support the ingestion, analysis, and reporting of advertising delivery and revenue data
Support ad-hoc requests from various internal teams (Accounting, Legal, Licensing, Financial Planning, etc) as well as external podcast publishers that require analysis of advertising data and systems
Work with a cross-functional team of data scientists, engineers, and finance representatives to define and test requirements for enhancing revenue recognition systems and data products
Work with a group of highly motivated individuals who are passionate about Spotify's success
Who You Are
A minimum 6 years of experience using databases and analytics tools to solve business problems
Experience managing and developing a team of data analysts / scientists
Degree in information systems, mathematics, statistics, computer science, or another quantitative discipline
Excellent verbal, written and interpersonal skills
Ability to prioritize and deliver results in a fast moving company with a wide variety of strategic initiatives
Previous experience working with advertising delivery data and relevant systems such as ad servers is ideal
Technical proficiency in SQL, Python / Pandas, Big Query / Google Cloud Platform, Tableau, Qliksense (or other visualization tools), Basic Command Line Operations
Where You'll Be
Hybrid role based in our New York offices (average 2 to 3 days a week required)
Working hours? We operate within the Eastern time zone for collaboration
The United States base range for this position is $140,096-$200,137 plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, 13 paid flexible holidays, paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future.

description:
Together, we innovate for a stronger Colorado
The work of employees at the Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT) is challenging and diverse because the needs of agencies, customers and Coloradans constantly evolve. But our focus never changes: improve the lives of all Coloradans through innovation and collaboration. We're building one of the nation's leading government IT organizations by reimagining how we support agencies, building first-of-their-kind applications, and creating an inclusive, collaborative culture, together. Join us in the important work of providing equitable access to services.


Watch this video to learn more about how we're Serving People. Serving Colorado.
IMPORTANT NOTE: Please review your application to ensure completion. For the most equitable applicant experience, OIT's hiring team considers only the contents of your application to review your qualifications. Please do not include any attachments (such as resume or cover letter) with your application as these items are not used by OIT's hiring team. 




Are you looking for an opportunity to apply your domain knowledge in education and workforce development with your keen analytic skills? If so, join us in making a meaningful impact in Colorado through innovative data analytics. As our new Data Scientist, you will be a key contributor in leveraging data to drive strategic business decisions for Colorado's Statewide Longitudinal Data System (SLDS), known as COdata. In this role, you will have the opportunity to employ advanced analytics techniques using modern data tools such as Snowflake, Python, SQL, R, and Tableau, as you conduct comprehensive data analysis spanning descriptive, diagnostic, and predictive methodologies. 


You will closely collaborate with the Data Architects, Data Engineers, Data Visualization Developers, Senior Management, OIT leadership, and agency stakeholders to develop sophisticated data visualizations, automated reporting processes, and actionable insights that inform and improve business outcomes. If using your creativity and innovation in the development and delivery of impactful data initiatives is what you love, apply today for the chance to also put your passion into the state you love! 


Some of the key responsibilities include:


Design useful education to career research questions and appropriate quantitative methods to inform policy and practice.


Conduct quantitative research on administrative data sets. 


Write research reports, briefs, infographics and slides deck to convey results. 


Design, maintain and optimize visualization dashboards in Tableau.


Combining data from multiple sources to produce meaningful metrics.


Identify data patterns, trends and communicate those key insights as recommended actions to key audiences .


Developing and maintaining complex dashboards and reports using Tableau, visualizing data sourced from Snowflake and other data repositories.


Communicating complex data insights and analytical findings to technical and non-technical stakeholders effectively.


Ensuring data quality and governance standards are met within the Snowflake environment.


Utilizing Python and SQL to extract, transform, and load (ETL) within Snowflake for analysis.


Working with resource managers and stakeholders to identify and integrate new data sources.


Leading and participating in cross-functional teams to develop data-driven solutions.


Present information and findings in a way that is accessible to both SLDS staff and the general public.


Oversee the production, display, and development of data structures and analytics for the Colorado SLDS.


Ensure data privacy and security in alignment with CISO guidelines. 


A wide salary range is posted for this position and any job offer is based upon a salary analysis to comply with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act. The salary analysis considers relevant experience, education, certifications, and state seniority as compared to others doing substantially similar work. While all offers are compliant with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, there is no guarantee an offer will be at the top of the posted range based on the salary analysis. 

This is a skills-based job announcement. The required minimum qualifications and/or education (if substituting for the proven experience, knowledge, and skills), are as follows: 

Minimum Qualifications:


A minimum of five (5) years working experience as a Data Analyst in the public sector of either education or workforce development, with significant expertise in using Snowflake, Python, SQL, R, and Tableau.


A minimum of three (3) years of experience developing dashboards using data reporting tools (Tableau - preferred, Power BI, R Shiny or PyShiny).

Deep understanding of applied research methods, specifically program evaluation and quantitative data analysis of longitudinal in the public sector data. 

At least five (5) years experience working with education and/or workforce data. 

Experience in conducting descriptive, diagnostic, and predictive data analysis in the public sector.


Strong understanding of data modeling, database management, SQL, and ETL processes in the public sector.



Substitutions:

Additional appropriate education will substitute for the required experience on a year-for-year basis, but cannot completely substitute for these qualifications. 

Training or Certification related to the work assigned to the position will be assigned credit towards substitution for experience and/or education, but cannot completely substitute for these qualifications. 

If the minimum qualifications include a degree requirement, additional appropriate paid or unpaid experience will substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis.


Preferred Qualifications:


Domain knowledge of education to career data and analyses.


Experience working for an SLDS.


Experience working for a governmental organization. 


Experience designing, building, implementing, and maintaining data and system integrations and data transformations utilizing Snowflake.


Familiarity with data governance frameworks and tools, including Informatica.


Knowledge of other cloud platforms like AWS, GCP or Azure.



Conditions of Employment:

OIT employees must comply with any screening procedures in place at state agency locations where they might perform work. 

A pre-employment background check will be conducted as part of the selection process. Post-employment background checks will be required for specific agencies as business needs dictate, which may include a polygraph exam, fingerprint-based criminal history search, reference checks, and a drug test.

This position may require travel within the specified geographic area, and to locations across the state as needed. 

If this posting indicates “remote from anywhere in CO” in the title, periodic reporting to the primary state work location designated for the position is required. All remote work must be performed in Colorado. 


While candidates from out of state will be considered for this role, the candidate selected for the position must relocate and reside in Colorado on the first day of their new position. A reasonable timeframe for relocation will be established on an individual basis, while considering business needs, and determining a start date.
